name: Mucocutaneous Venous Malformations
aliases: Venous Malformation of Skin and Mucosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Venous Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, bluish mucocutaneous lesions
MRI or ultrasound showing slow-flow venous channels without arterial involvement
Biopsy demonstrating dilated, thin-walled venous channels lined by endothelium
Doppler ultrasound confirming absence of arterial flow within lesion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical mucocutaneous lesions with confirmatory imaging showing slow-flow venous malformation without arterial involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not mandatory if clinical and imaging findings are conclusive

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located on lips, oral mucosa, or skin
searchTerms: soft blue skin or mouth spots
compressible bluish lesions on skin or mucosa
soft bluish lumps on skin or mouth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lesion enlargement with dependency or Valsalva maneuver
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic distension on increased venous pressure
searchTerms: lesion grows when standing or straining
swelling increases with position or pressure
mass enlarges with dependency or Valsalva

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness at lesion site
common.notes: Often due to thrombosis or trauma

searchTerms: bleeding from mouth or skin lesions

common.notes: Due to slow venous blood flow

occasional.notes: May cause acute pain and swelling
searchTerms: blood clots in vein within lesion
vein inflammation with clots in lesion

occasional.symptomName: Ulceration of overlying skin or mucosa
searchTerms: skin or mouth sore over tumor
open sore on skin or mucous membrane

occasional.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion size
occasional.notes: May affect speech or mastication if oral
searchTerms: difficulty using area due to lesion size
small stones in veins of lesion

rare.notes: Rare but possible in extensive lesions

laboratory: Normal blood counts unless bleeding or thrombosis present
D-dimer may be elevated if thrombosis occurs
imaging: MRI showing lobulated, slow-flow venous channels
Doppler ultrasound demonstrating compressible, hypoechoic lesions with venous flow
Phleboliths visible as calcifications on X-ray or CT
other: Histopathology showing dilated, thin-walled venous channels lined by endothelial cells

distinguishingFeatures: Rapid postnatal growth followed by involution
Bright red color rather than bluish
Presence of arterial flow on Doppler

redFlags: Neurological symptoms if lesion compresses nerves
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.

Boon LM, Mulliken JB, Vikkula M. Pathogenesis of vascular anomalies. Clin Plast Surg. 1998;25(3):381-394.
